newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese industry presents budget requests.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese industry presents budget requests.

text.p: Portuguese industrialists asked the government to cut corporate taxes and for more tax relief on investments in budget proposals announced on Monday.

The Portuguese Industry Association called for tax relief on investment to be doubled to 20 percent from 10 percent. It wants company tax cut to 35 percent from 38.5 percent and a step-by-step reduction in the double taxation of profits and dividends.

The Socialist government is drawing up plans to cut the budget deficit to three percent in 1997 to meet a key target for entry to the European Union's single currency. The deficit is expected to be around four percent in 1996.
Companies operating in developing areas of Portugal should be taxed at a flat 20 percent, it said.
Other measures included an end to corporation or Value Added Tax (VAT) on European subsidies and halving the stamp duty on bank transactions to three percent.
